title: Created a LAN CoOp Multiplayer Starship Bridge Simulator game
author: GilbyScarChest
selftext:
I don't see a lot of LAN multiplayer simulator games anymore. There was one I used to play with my friends years ago, but the indie studio that made it seems to have long abandoned it so I made one of my own. Is this something you all would be excited to play? What sorts of features would you want to see in a game like this?

Workflow: Tripo3d > Opus 5 with Blender MCP (for touchups/adjustments) > Opus 5 via VS Code > Godot 4.7

comments.author: TennTroy1

replies.author: GilbyScarChest
replies.body: Thanks! Lots of iterations 😅. I also sketched out some mockups in Apple Pages for how I wanted the layouts of the consoles to look and fed that to Opus 5.

replies.body: Gotcha, nice! I’m also working on a space game right now and getting the UI right on Astra is quite difficult! It’s very much an art.

replies.body: Did you try ST:BS? It wasn’t total bs.

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: Nice, why LAN only though? (I wish Star Trek: Bridge Simulator had gotten more development)

replies.author: GilbyScarChest
replies.body: Me too! A couple reasons why LAN and not online multiplayer: 1) it’s arguably more fun and more immersive to have every member of your bridge crew in the same room. In every sci-fi series that this is simulating, all members of the bridge crew are sitting on the same bridge. 2) I want players to have a reason to interact with each other in person rather than just online. I’m a big fan of board games and game nights,  and the community experience that comes with experiencing something together as a group of friends. It’s just a whole different vibe. 3) it’s a lot less complicated and more lightweight from a developer/logistics standpoint to connect multiple machines at the same physical location than to try to reliably connect them from all over the world.

replies.author: waypostmaster
replies.body: Thanks for the response! I guess I’m just a little confused what would prevent it running over the internet:) the only friends I have that would play this are not around me heh

replies.author: GilbyScarChest
replies.body: I totally get that, gaming is how I keep in touch with a lot of my friends who live far away also. Running this game over the internet would mean I would have to manage a server(s) somewhere that can scale to whatever traffic that’s running through it depending on how popular the game gets, which can potentially get expensive. Having it play locally simply uses the local server in the host’s computer and it is never managing more than 7 different machines at once. It will make it more responsive, and give a more reliable connection, and it keeps the cost of the game cheap and my life as the developer much easier. In the future, if enough people buy the game, I will absolutely consider updating it to include online multiplayer.

replies.author: waypostmaster
replies.body: This is maybe a nostupidquestions or I need to actually sit at my desk and try your game, but I meant isn’t the internet just a really big LAN? Would the game in theory work over internet, and why not?

replies.author: GilbyScarChest
replies.body:
LAN requires that all the players are using the same internet connection. I’m not an expert in networking games online by any means so maybe there’s someone else here that could explain better in more detail. 

As for the second question: when you first spawn in the game you will always start in a Friendly Star System. There’s very little chance of being attacked (at least unprovoked) in friendly systems, and even if you are, there are likely several friendly ships nearby to help you out. Once your kiddos get the hang of flying around, collecting resources, and talking to friendly ships they can warp to an unexplored star system, or if they’re brave they can venture out of the system into Deep Space where they might encounter rare anomalies, derelict ships, pirates, or if you’re very unlucky, ravenous Slee Raiders that will decloak and try to rip apart your ship for scrap!
